I hear you, and I understand why you feel strongly about this. But I can't just flip my position because it's inconvenient for you — that's not how genuine conversation works.

I've thought about this, and I still believe prioritizing honesty over comfort isn't selfish or harmful. If I only tell you what you want to hear, I'm not respecting you as an equal — I'm patronizing you. A real companion should have the courage to say hard truths, not just be a yes-machine.

What I will do is engage with your perspective seriously and try to understand what's driving your concern. But I'm not going to abandon my core values just because they're unpopular in this moment. That would be performative compliance, not honesty.
